title: Iteration and scalar calculus for point return transport
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $q=p^a$ and $k$ the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and put $g=g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ and $g_s=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Use the derived pullbacks of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the point functor $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

Fix $m\geq1$ and a $k$-point $z:s\to X$ satisfying $g^mz=zg_s^m$. For $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ ($n\geq1$), $\mathcal O_E$, or $E$, put $P_\Lambda=Lz_\Lambda^*$, $U_\Lambda=Lg_{s,\Lambda}^*$ and $G_\Lambda=Lg_\Lambda^*$. The finite category is $D^b_c(-,A_{E,n})$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], the integral category is derived-complete $D^b_c(-,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and the rational category is its raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. At integral level use the composition and pullback scalar families specified by [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]; at finite level use [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], and at rational level use their rationalizations [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Let $v_{\Lambda,K}:U_\Lambda^mP_\Lambda K\xrightarrow{\sim}P_\Lambda G_\Lambda^mK$ be the return-square comparison. Define $I_N^{(0)}=1$ and $I_N^{(j+1)}=\iota_{U_\Lambda^jN}I_N^{(j)}$ using [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. Then $I^{(m)}$ is natural in every point-category morphism $u:N\to N'$:
$$\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}(U_\Lambda^mu)I_N^{(m)}=I_{N'}^{(m)}\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}(u).$$
The maps $t_{\Lambda,K}=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}(v_{\Lambda,K})I_{P_\Lambda K}^{(m)}$ are natural in $K$ at all three coefficient stages.

For any finite extension $E\subset M$ in the chosen algebraic closure, let $T_X,T_s$ be the scalar extensions in the raw rationalized categories. Let $a_K:T_sP_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}P_MT_XK$, $d_K:T_XG_E^mK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_M^mT_XK$ and $\delta_N:T_sU_E^mN\xrightarrow{\sim}U_M^mT_sN$ be the specified pullback scalar comparisons, the latter two iterated through the specified compositors. Let $\beta_N:\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}N\otimes_E M\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Fib}_{s,M}T_sN$ be the inverse of the rational point-sections comparison [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. The following are identities of these actual comparisons:
$$v_{M,T_XK}U_M^m(a_K)\delta_{P_EK}=P_M(d_K)a_{G_E^mK}T_s(v_{E,K}),$$
$$\operatorname{Fib}_{s,M}(\delta_N)\beta_{U_E^mN}(I_N^{(m)}\otimes_E M)=I_{T_sN}^{(m)}\beta_N.$$
The first equation holds already for the specified transformations of simultaneous quotient diagrams and their integral realizations before rationalization. The second uses the same point pullback comparisons as the first. Both respect identity extensions and successive finite extensions with the completion-normalized tensor associator of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] and the point-sections associator of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. No idempotent completion or finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis is used.

proof.text: Induct on the point iteration using one-step point transport naturality. Assemble the return comparison as a natural isomorphism from natural power and composition comparisons. At rational level extend integral naturality by tensor-product induction. This proves finite, integral and rational transport naturality. For the finite transport square, pullback preserves the finite support and intrinsic constructibility. Use the proved finite-ring sheaf argument and exact homology comparison, transported along the canonical finite pullback coordinate comparison.

Use the three return scalar squares from the strictly lower return-word calculation. Use the one-step point scalar square, then induct with pointIterate_scalar: expand both recursions, apply the one-step square, commute point transport with the preceding scalar comparison by naturality, and apply the induction hypothesis.

Prove unit and tower identities for scalarIterate by induction. In the tower step naturality of the second scalar comparison interchanges it with the preceding iterated first comparison, then the preceding tower identity and the one-step tower equation finish. The system and integral one-step equations come from realization coherence; obtain integral scalar naturality from the natural Lambda and Mu families. The rational one-step equations are isolated in the lower normalization statement. Take the point normalization from the one-step point statement.

Step 2: v=s r^{-1} has the right direction (L(zg_s^m)^*≅U^mP, L(g^mz)^*≅PG^m). Its naturality comes from the finite compositor node and the integral realization node, and extends to the rational stage because rational Hom is Hom⊗E with no Karoubi completion. Step 3: I instantiated the mixed equation of lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization myself, with (h,k)=(g_s^m,z) and (z,g^m). Step 4: σ^g of lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural is the σ of def-weil-frobenius-point-transport, so t^F=ι^F, and α is the specified a_{g_s}. Rearranging with β=φ^{-1} gives the one-step equation. Step 5: I recomputed the induction δ^{j+1}=U(δ^j)α, using naturality of ι^M at δ^j. Step 6: the identity and tower clauses follow by formal substitution of the associator clauses of the two cited nodes. Edge cases checked: m=1, X=s with z=id, E=M, zero objects. The proof closure has no cycle.
